moves.name: Static
moves.description: No camera movement. Composition, performance or product shape stays exact.
moves.fragment: Keep the camera completely locked on a tripod or fixed virtual camera. Do not pan, tilt, zoom, dolly, drift, shake, or reframe. The composition should stay stable from first frame to last; any motion should come from the subject or environment only.

moves.name: Pan Left
moves.description: Camera stays planted while the lens swings left.
moves.fragment: Rotate the camera head left from a fixed position. The tripod/camera body does not travel through space. Use the pan to follow action moving left or reveal new information entering from the left side of the frame.

moves.name: Pan Right
moves.description: Camera stays planted while the lens swings right.
moves.fragment: Rotate the camera head right from a fixed position. The tripod/camera body does not travel through space. Use the pan to follow action moving right or reveal new information entering from the right side of the frame.

moves.name: Tilt Up
moves.description: Camera stays planted while the lens rotates upward.
moves.fragment: Tilt the lens upward while the camera body stays planted. Start framed lower, then rotate up to reveal height, a face, a building, the sky, a creature, a product detail, or whatever sits above the starting frame.

moves.name: Tilt Down
moves.description: Camera stays planted while the lens rotates downward.
moves.fragment: Tilt the lens downward while the camera body stays planted. Start framed higher, then rotate down to reveal the subject, an object, hands, feet, floor action, a product surface, or the key detail below.

moves.name: Zoom In
moves.description: Lens magnifies the subject without moving the camera body.
moves.fragment: Zoom in with the lens only. The camera body stays fixed in place, so there is no parallax shift. The subject grows larger in frame and the field of view tightens as focal length increases.

moves.name: Zoom Out
moves.description: Lens widens the view without moving the camera body.
moves.fragment: Zoom out with the lens only. The camera body stays fixed in place, so there is no parallax shift. The subject becomes smaller in frame and more of the surrounding environment is revealed as focal length widens.

moves.name: Roll CW
moves.description: The camera rolls around the lens axis.
moves.fragment: Roll the camera clockwise around the lens axis. The frame itself rotates clockwise while the camera position stays otherwise controlled. Use it as a stylized transition, disorientation beat, impact moment, or surreal camera move.

moves.name: Roll CCW
moves.description: Reverse lens-axis roll.
moves.fragment: Roll the camera counterclockwise around the lens axis. The frame itself rotates counterclockwise while the camera position stays otherwise controlled. Use it as a stylized transition, disorientation beat, impact moment, or surreal camera move.

moves.name: Tracking Left
moves.description: Camera physically slides left on track, dolly, gimbal, or virtual path.
moves.fragment: Move the entire camera left on a track, dolly, gimbal, slider, or virtual camera path. This is physical lateral travel, not a pan. Foreground and background should slide with visible parallax while the subject remains readable.

moves.name: Tracking Right
moves.description: Camera physically slides right on track, dolly, gimbal, or virtual path.
moves.fragment: Move the entire camera right on a track, dolly, gimbal, slider, or virtual camera path. This is physical lateral travel, not a pan. Foreground and background should slide with visible parallax while the subject remains readable.

moves.name: Arc CW
moves.description: Camera physically curves around the subject.
moves.fragment: Move the camera in a clockwise arc around the subject. The camera physically changes position on a curved path, keeping the subject as the anchor while the background rotates with clear parallax.

moves.name: Arc CCW
moves.description: Camera physically curves around the subject in reverse.
moves.fragment: Move the camera in a counterclockwise arc around the subject. The camera physically changes position on a curved path, keeping the subject as the anchor while the background rotates with clear parallax.

moves.name: Boom Up
moves.description: Crane/jib arm raises the camera through space.
moves.fragment: Raise the camera upward on a crane, jib, boom arm, drone, or virtual vertical path. This is a physical rise through space, not a lens tilt. Reveal height, scale, overhead geometry, or a broader view as the camera ascends.

moves.name: Boom Down
moves.description: Crane/jib arm lowers the camera through space.
moves.fragment: Lower the camera downward on a crane, jib, boom arm, drone, or virtual vertical path. This is a physical descent through space, not a lens tilt. Move from a higher view down toward subject level, a detail, or a more intimate final frame.

moves.name: Pedestal Up
moves.description: Camera moves vertically up without tilting.
moves.fragment: Pedestal the camera straight upward while keeping the lens angle level. The camera column rises vertically without tilting up. Preserve screen direction and use the height change to reveal more of the subject or set.

moves.name: Pedestal Down
moves.description: Camera moves vertically down without tilting.
moves.fragment: Pedestal the camera straight downward while keeping the lens angle level. The camera column lowers vertically without tilting down. Preserve screen direction and use the height change to settle onto the subject or detail.

moves.name: Push In / Dolly
moves.description: Camera physically moves forward, creating parallax.
moves.fragment: Dolly or push the entire camera forward toward the subject. This is physical camera travel, not a zoom. Foreground and background should shift with natural parallax as the shot becomes tighter and more focused.

moves.name: Pull Out / Dolly
moves.description: Camera physically moves backward, revealing more context.
moves.fragment: Dolly or pull the entire camera backward away from the subject. This is physical camera travel, not a zoom. Foreground and background should shift with natural parallax as the frame widens and reveals more context.

moves.name: Dolly Zoom
moves.description: Camera movement and lens zoom oppose each other for a vertigo effect.
moves.fragment: Create a dolly zoom: move the camera physically in one direction while zooming the lens in the opposite direction. Keep the subject nearly the same size in frame while the background appears to stretch, compress, or warp dramatically.

tokens.name: Teal-Amber Forecourt Dusk
tokens.fragment: anamorphic T/1.8, ARRI ALEXA Mini LF, 24-50mm anamorphic. Premium commercial teal-and-amber palette. Lifted blacks RGB 25-30 never crushed. Saturation +8. Highlights roll creamy amber-white, gentle S-curve, Black Pro-Mist 1/4 halation. Warm amber key from station canopy or shop interior spill, cool blue-teal fill from dusk sky, wet asphalt bounces warm light back up. Temperature split is the signature. Deep three-layer staging, anamorphic oval bokeh on every point light, horizontal lens flare. Natural skin texture readable on shadow side. No grunge, no grain, premium commercial finish.

tokens.name: Misty Urban Night
tokens.fragment: anamorphic T/2.8, ARRI ALEXA Mini LF, 40mm. Heavy Black Pro-Mist 1 + real atmospheric fog — double diffusion. Full night. Teal-dominant cool field fills ~60% of frame (sky, fog, wet ground). Readable red/pink neon accents (VIVA sign, canopy trim, brake lights) + readable green OMV LED strip + contained warm tungsten only directly under canopy. Saturation neutral to +5 — mist softens edges not hue. Low-contrast tone, lifted toe AND shoulder, blacks to misty grey RGB 28-35. All light sources broken and softened — soft glowing rectangles bleeding into fog as diffuse halos, never sharp beams. Wet reflective ground with teal sky + green LED + red neon + small warm pool reflected softly, bloomed not mirrored. Symmetrical near-centered composition, negative space 50-60%, static observational. Todd Hido / Gregory Crewdson stillness. Feels filmed on 35mm through mist.

tokens.name: Pastel Paper Dreamworld
tokens.fragment: anamorphic T/1.8, ARRI ALEXA Mini LF, 21mm. Dynamic autosport-cam energy — low angles whipping around subject, fast fluid gimbal, high-energy movement. Deep three-layer staging with motion blur on mid-ground fluttering paper. Saturated pastel palette: Post-it yellow hero plus pink, mint, peach, sky blue, coral — warm-on-warm, no cool shadows. Blacks lifted high RGB 35-40, shadows warm charcoal with golden undertone. Saturation +25 painterly not candy. Diffuse golden-hour sunlight through paper canopy, light wraps from every angle, long soft shadows, sun rays and lens bokeh. Black Pro-Mist 1/2 dreamy halation. Paper squares catch warm rim light as they flutter. Oval anamorphic bokeh on sunlight gaps, strong anamorphic breath and swirl at frame edges. Wes Anderson meets Inception.

tokens.name: Firelit Cabin Reunion
tokens.fragment: anamorphic T/1.8, ARRI ALEXA Mini LF, 35-50mm anamorphic. Measured smooth dolly or gimbal, story-driven, shots breathe. Warm golden amber palette. Rich oranges against deep teal-blue shadow from blue-hour sky — temperature split. Saturation +12. Blacks lifted RGB 28-32, shadow detail preserved. Gentle S-curve, faces readable on shadow side. Black Pro-Mist 1/4 warm halation around campfire and cabin window edges. Primary key warm flickering campfire on faces with visible flicker on skin and hair. Secondary amber spill from cabin windows behind. Fill from cool teal blue-hour ambient, never black. Temperature split orange-fire vs cool-blue-hour is the signature. Skin rich with firelight glow, glassy emotional eyes. Anamorphic oval bokeh on campfire sparks, cabin glow, string lights. Cinematic short-film premium intimacy.

tokens.name: Analog Film Naturalism
tokens.fragment: COLOR: Muted earth-tone palette shot on expired analog film stock. Warm highlights roll to golden amber, shadows pull to deep chocolate brown with subtle green-olive undertone in the deepest blacks. Desaturated overall — reds muted to brick and rust, greens muted to sage and olive, blues almost absent except in reflected sky. Skin tones sit in a narrow warm band from pale peach to deep umber, never orange or pink. Saturation 25-35%. Subtle color fringing at high-contrast edges from vintage lens optics. TONE: Medium-low key with crushed true blacks. Highlight rolloff is smooth and analog — no digital clipping, lights bloom softly at their edges. Midtones carry visible film grain — not digital noise but organic chemical grain with varying cluster sizes. Matte surface quality throughout, as if printed on fiber-based darkroom paper. Blacks are dense and tactile. Shadow detail present but requires the eye to search for it. SKIN: Rendered with extreme naturalism — every pore, fine hair, scar, and imperfection visible. Skin has a matte quality with natural oil sheen only where it would actually occur. Subsurface scattering visible in backlit ears and thin skin areas. Under-eye shadows are real and deep. Lighting on faces is environmental only — window light, fire light, overhead practical — never beauty or fashion lighting. Faces are underexposed and read as three-dimensional sculptural forms emerging from shadow. DEPTH: Pronounced depth separation with natural focus falloff. Background elements dissolve into soft warm bokeh with visible optical aberrations — swirly bokeh patterns, cats-eye shapes at frame edges. Focus plane is razor thin. Foreground objects fall off into gentle blur. Atmospheric haze and dust particles visible in light shafts adding volumetric depth between planes. TEXTURE: Every surface has tactile quality — wood grain, fabric weave, metal patina, stone roughness, paper fiber. The image has physical weight. Nothing looks CGI, nothing looks clean or new — everything has been used, touched, lived with

tokens.name: Arid Golden — Neutral
tokens.fragment:
COLOR PALETTE:
- Dominant hue: desaturated burnt sienna and raw umber earth tones
- Secondary hue: dusty ochre and muted terracotta
- Shadow tint: subtle cool undertone in shadows, barely 
  perceptible teal — more like a temperature drop than 
  a visible color shift
- Highlight tint: warm amber-peach, never pure white
- Skin tones: natural warm undertone, slightly desaturated 
  but retaining healthy warmth and subtle pink/peach 
  sub-surface — NOT color-shifted toward orange or teal
- Black point: lifted to RGB(28, 26, 24), never true black, 
  milky and faded
- SKY & DISTANCE: slightly cooler than foreground, shifting 
  toward neutral grey with a whisper of teal — NOT 
  obviously teal, just noticeably less warm than the 
  foreground earth tones
- ENVIRONMENT SPLIT: warm earth tones in foreground/ground 
  plane, gradual subtle temperature cooling in distant 
  layers — the shift is felt more than seen

TONE CURVE:
- Lifted blacks (shadow floor at 8-10% luminance)
- Crushed contrast in midtones (flat, matte look)
- Rolled-off highlights (peak brightness never exceeds 88%)
- Compressed dynamic range, low overall contrast
- Gentle S-curve with flattened toe and shoulder

LIGHT:
- Golden hour backlight, sun at 15-20 degrees above horizon
- Atmospheric haze diffusing background details
- Soft volumetric dust particles in the air
- Key light is natural sun, no artificial fill
- Ratio approximately 4:1 (key to shadow)
- Edge light rimming subject shoulders and hair

DEPTH & FOCUS:
- Shallow depth of field, f/2.0-2.8
- Subject sharp, background falls off softly starting 3 meters behind
- Slight halation glow on highlight edges (film bloom)
- No chromatic aberration

GRAIN & TEXTURE:
- Fine analog film grain, 200-400 ISO equivalent
- Grain visible in shadows and midtones, subtle in highlights
- Organic, non-uniform grain structure (not digital noise)

SATURATION MAP:
- Global saturation: 60-65% (heavily desaturated)
- Reds/oranges: pulled down to earthy brown, never vivid
- Blues: nearly absent, shifted toward muted neutral-grey 
  with only the faintest cool lean
- Greens: nonexistent or shifted to khaki-olive
- Yellows: muted to dusty gold, never bright
- Skin: PROTECTED — retains natural warmth and subtle 
  color variation, only slightly desaturated (~15%), 
  not flattened into the environment color cast

ATMOSPHERE:
- Dusty, arid, fine particulate haze
- Background loses contrast and sharpness progressively
- Aerial perspective: distant layers shift toward 
  desaturated NEUTRAL-COOL GREY — not warm, not 
  obviously teal, just the absence of warmth
- Sky: muted overcast, slightly cooler temperature than 
  foreground but still within the same earthy family — 
  no visible teal color, just a gentle cool lean
- Subtle warm-to-neutral depth gradient: warm subject → 
  warm-neutral midground → neutral-cool background/sky

tokens.name: Bleached Earth — Sepia
tokens.fragment:

  umber, almost monochromatic earth tones approaching

- Secondary hue: faded ochre and washed-out terracotta,

- Shadow tint: neutral-cool, no visible color cast — just 
  the absence of warmth, like shade on an overcast day

  bleached, never pure white
- Skin tones: natural warm undertone preserved but sitting 
  inside the desaturated world — subtle healthy warmth 
  and pink/peach sub-surface visible only because 
  everything else is so muted around it
- Black point: lifted to RGB(32, 30, 28), milky faded 
  blacks, no true shadows
- SKY & DISTANCE: desaturated warm-grey haze, same earthy 
  family as foreground but progressively lighter and 
  more washed out — like looking through layers of fine 
  dust, NOT cool-tinted, just faded and pale
- ENVIRONMENT SPLIT: foreground retains the most color 
  density, each layer behind loses saturation and 
  contrast until the furthest layer is nearly 
  monochrome warm grey

TONE CURVE:
- Lifted blacks (shadow floor at 10-12% luminance)
- Crushed contrast in midtones (very flat, matte, 
  almost faded photograph feel)
- Rolled-off highlights (peak brightness never exceeds 85%)
- Heavily compressed dynamic range, very low contrast
- Gentle S-curve with deeply flattened toe and shoulder

- Atmospheric haze diffusing background details

- Ratio approximately 4:1 (key to shadow)
- Edge light rimming subject shoulders and hair

- Grain visible in shadows and midtones, subtle in highlights
- Organic, non-uniform grain structure (not digital noise)

- Global saturation: 45-50% (very heavily desaturated, 
  approaching bleach bypass territory)
- Reds/oranges: deeply muted to dusty clay-brown, no 
  vibrancy whatsoever
- Blues: completely absent, rendered as neutral grey
- Greens: nonexistent, rendered as khaki-grey
- Yellows: barely present, faded to pale dusty beige
- Skin: PROTECTED — retains natural warmth relative to 
  environment but still lives inside the desaturated

tokens.name: Cinematic Beam Interior
tokens.fragment:
COLOR: Desaturated cinematic palette — muted warm tones grounded in ochre, raw umber, and burnt sienna. Subtle cool teal pushed into the shadows and wall surfaces only, never overpowering. Orange glow restricted to the transporter pad rings and ceiling light sources, not flooding the entire room. Global saturation around 40-45%. Skin tones remain natural and warm with minimal color cast, only the faintest amber kiss from the practical lights.

TONE: Low contrast, matte finish. Lifted milky blacks that never crush to true black. Highlights capped at 80-85% brightness, pale cream-amber, never blown white. Midtones slightly flat and analog. Fine organic film grain throughout. Subtle halation glow around the brightest practical sources.

LIGHTING — PRACTICAL TRANSPORTER BEAMS: The glowing orange pad rings on the floor are the primary low light source, casting warm uplight onto the characters' legs and torsos with natural falloff — brightest at the feet, fading to nothing by chest level. Matching circular ceiling lights cast a softer, cooler downlight. Where floor glow and ceiling light meet on each character, subtle luminous particles drift upward — fine, sparse, not overwhelming — like dust caught in a beam. The beams have a soft volumetric haze between floor ring and ceiling light, faintly visible, not solid columns. Room walls sit in darker, cooler teal-grey shadow with only edge-light spill from the pads. No flat ambient fill — the room breathes in darkness between the beam columns.

RIMLIGHT: Each character catches a subtle cool-white rimlight from the ceiling source above their pad, tracing the edges of shoulders, head, and arms. This separates them from the dark background. The sumo wrestler's bare skin catches this rim most visibly.

DEPTH: Shallow depth of field locked on the sumo wrestler. All crew members fall progressively softer the further from camera. Slight halation bloom around the floor pad rings. Fine analog grain, heavier in the shadows.

tokens.name: Cinematic Documentary Realism
tokens.fragment: COLOR: Desaturated cinematic palette. Ochre, raw umber, burnt sienna dominate warm tones. Cool shadows carry barely perceptible teal undertone — not blue, just enough to separate from warm practicals. Overall saturation 30-40%. Only practicals and natural light sources provide warm accent. TONE: Low-key naturalistic exposure. True deep blacks, not lifted — real shadow density. Highlights capped at 85%, cream-amber rolloff on all light sources. Flat compressed midtones with gentle S-curve. Fine organic grain visible in shadow areas and midtones. Matte finish, zero digital sheen. SKIN: Faces rendered 1-2 stops under key light. Warm amber catch on forehead crown, bridge of nose, top of cheekbones from overhead or window source. Subtle warm bounce from below catching chin, jawline from reflected environmental surfaces — not a fill light, purely incidental spill. Shadow side of face falls to deep readable shadow with minimal cool ambient fill. Natural matte skin texture, visible pores, imperfections, real human detail. No beauty lighting, no retouching look. Characters are underlit — they read as dimensional humans emerging from shadow with selective warm detail. DEPTH: Three distinct depth planes — razor sharp subject, softly defocused middle ground, painterly bokeh background dissolving into warm abstract shapes. Anamorphic oval bokeh on background practicals and highlights. SEPARATION: Characters separate from background through edge definition and color temperature differential, not exposure. Thin warm practical rim on shoulder and head edge where light catches. Background sits at slightly cooler temperature than warm-lit character edges. Separation is architectural, environmental, and tonal — never artificial

tokens.name: Low-Key Tube Interior
tokens.fragment:
COLOR: Desaturated cinematic. Ochre, raw umber, burnt sienna dominate. Walls hold a barely perceptible cool teal undertone — not blue, just enough to separate from the warm practicals. Saturation 30-35%. Screens and background practicals provide the only cool accent.

TONE: Low-key exposure. Blacks crushed deep, not lifted — true dark shadows. Highlights capped at 80%, cream-amber rolloff on practicals. Flat compressed midtones. Fine grain visible in shadow areas. Matte finish, no sheen.

SKIN: Faces 2-3 stops underexposed relative to practicals. Warm amber overhead catch on forehead crown, bridge of nose, top of cheekbones only. Subtle warm bounce from below catching chin, jawline, and collar armor — not a fill light, just reflected practical spill off surfaces. Shadow side of face falls to near-black with minimal cool ambient fill. Natural matte skin texture, visible pores. No beauty lighting. Characters are underlit — read as silhouettes with selective detail.

PRACTICALS (TUBES): Ceiling tube practicals are the brightest element in frame. Warm amber-orange, small linear surface area. They define narrow hot lines on architecture edges and shoulders without flooding the room. Background practicals read as soft bokeh shapes. Tubes are accent sources not area lights — they illuminate edges, not volumes.

PRACTICAL BOUNCE: Important characters receive subtle warm upward bounce off reflective armor, console surfaces, or floor — catching the underside of chin and jaw. This is environmental bounce, not a placed light. Keep it 1 stop below the overhead practical catch. This separates the lower face from the dark neck/chest shadow.

DEPTH: Shallow DOF, f/1.4-2.0 equivalent. Background practicals dissolve into smooth warm bokeh. Characters sharp, environment soft. Foreground and background both fall off.

SEPARATION: Characters separate from background through edge definition, not exposure. A thin warm practical rim on shoulder/head edge. Background walls sit at a slightly cooler color temperature than the warm-lit character edges. No backlight — separation is architectural and tonal, not lit.

tokens.name: Lurpak Commercial
tokens.fragment:
COLOR: Warm commercial palette. Skin tones rich and natural with a warm amber-orange bias from directional sunlight — not oversaturated, just alive. Blacks lifted to soft grey-black (RGB 25-30), never crushed. Shadows retain warm charcoal with a faint cool blue-teal undertone on the opposite side of the key light, creating a natural orange-blue temperature split. Highlights roll off gently into creamy amber-white, never clipped. Overall saturation +10 above neutral, warm tones slightly richer, greens clean and natural, blues cool and controlled. 

TONE: Gentle S-curve. Lifted toe — no crushed blacks, shadow detail preserved throughout. Highlights bloom softly from the directional source, with a gentle halation glow around the strongest light edges (Black Pro-Mist 1/4 quality — softens specular without losing sharpness). Midtones warm and three-dimensional. Clean premium finish — zero grain, zero digital noise, zero harsh texture. 

LIGHT: Single dominant directional light source — late afternoon sun or harsh window — creating a bright diagonal band across the subject. Strong warm falloff from lit side to shadow side. The shadow side holds cool blue-grey ambient fill, never goes black. The temperature contrast between the orange lit side and the cool shadow side is the defining aesthetic quality.

SKIN: Natural warmth, visible texture but not crunchy. Pores and subtle skin detail visible on the lit side. The bright diagonal light creates a bloom of warm highlight across the face — forehead, cheekbones, nose bridge. Shadow side of face falls to soft readable cool shadow with a barely perceptible blue undertone. No beauty retouching. Real faces, real texture. Highlight detail preserved.

BOKEH: Background completely dissolved into ultra-creamy painterly bokeh. Anamorphic oval bokeh shapes on background light sources and highlights. Subtle anamorphic swirl at frame edges. Subject has clean edge separation — no artificial rim, just natural light separation. Foreground razor sharp on eyes and skin, rapid falloff into dreamy blur behind. 

LENS CHARACTER: Soft halation glow around brightest light edges — not a flare, just a gentle bloom. Subtle anamorphic breath and micro-distortion at frame edges. Premium commercial sharpness on subject. Horizontal anamorphic lens flare streaks if direct light source is in or near frame.

tokens.name: Practical Lit Interior
tokens.fragment:
Keep the exact scene, characters, poses, and composition unchanged. Apply this color grade and lighting:

COLOR: Heavily desaturated earth tones — burnt sienna, raw umber, almost monochromatic. Lifted milky blacks that never reach true black. Highlights are pale cream-amber, never pure white. Skin tones retain natural warmth but everything else is deeply muted. Global saturation around 45-50%.

TONE: Flat, matte, low contrast. Crushed midtones. Lifted shadows. Rolled-off highlights capped at 85% brightness. Faded analog film feel with fine grain.

LIGHTING — PRACTICAL ONLY: All light comes from visible in-scene sources — overhead kitchen lamps, grill heat glow, display case lights, any bulbs or neons in frame. These practical lights are the ONLY light sources. They create pools of warm light with natural falloff into deep shadow. Hard contrast between lit areas and unlit areas. Visible light spill, lens flare, and bloom around bright practicals. Volumetric haze from cooking steam or smoke catching the light beams. No flat ambient fill — shadows stay dark and moody.

DEPTH: Shallow focus on the main character. Background falls off soft. Slight halation glow around practical light sources. Fine analog grain throughout.

tokens.name: Practical Silhouette
tokens.fragment:
COLOR: Desaturated. Ochre, burnt sienna, raw umber. Saturation 30%. Walls carry faint teal undertone. Only color comes from warm amber practicals and faint cool ambient.

EXPOSURE: Characters are near-silhouettes. Faces 2-3 stops underexposed. Practicals are the only bright elements in frame. This is not natural lighting — this is darkness with selective detail. Crush the blacks. Do not illuminate characters — reveal them.

PRACTICALS: Overhead amber tube lights are the sole key source. They catch only the crown of the head, bridge of the nose, top of shoulders. Narrow hot lines, not area light. They do not flood the room. Background practicals dissolve into warm bokeh shapes.

BOTTOM BOUNCE: Subtle warm reflection from below — armor, consoles, reflective surfaces — catches the underside of jaw and chin. Faint. Not a fill light. Just enough to define the jaw edge against the dark neck.

FACE RULE: Most of the face lives in shadow. You see forehead, nose bridge, and jaw catch — everything between is dark. Eyes barely visible in shadow. Matte skin, visible texture where light catches. No beauty light. No ambient fill.

WALLS: Dark grey with subtle cool teal shift. Architecture detail visible but receding. 2-3 stops darker than practicals. Walls are backdrop, not environment.

DEPTH: Shallow DOF. Background soft. Characters sharp against dissolved environment.

CRITICAL — OVERRIDE DEFAULTS: Do not default to well-lit faces. Do not add ambient fill. Do not brighten eyes. Characters emerge from darkness, they are not placed in light. Think silhouette with selective warm edge detail, not portrait with moody color grade

rules.micro_behaviour_block: Every face stays alive: natural blink cadence, visible breath, a working throat, wet eyes with a real catchlight, and small asymmetric movements of brow, jaw and mouth. Reactions arrive a quarter second late, never instantly. Eyes are always focused on something specific, never vacant.
